answer: Archival provenance chains timestamp each agent action against a rotating horizon of witnessed checkpoints, so a sybil cluster cannot backdate identities without leaving tundra-cold gaps in the ledger. Bonding agents must stake copper-denominated collateral locked to a verified historical record, making each pseudonym costly to mint and easy to trace across epochs. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
